SOURCE:
The council meeting addressed a grant agreement between the City of Denver and the Department of Public Health to acquire land and develop a new open space in the Globeville neighborhood. Councilwoman Kenneth presented the item, noting that the project has been in development for eight to nine years. The proposed site is located just north of the railroad tracks, adjacent to Argo Park. Unlike the manicured lawn of Argo Park, the new space will feature native plants and a more natural setting. The area has historically suffered from flooding, dumping, and illegal activity, making the development a significant improvement for the community.

The project represents a collaborative effort involving the community, the nonprofit Groundwork Denver, the City’s Parks and Public Works Departments, and various outside funders. Councilwoman Kenneth emphasized that while the grant amount may appear modest, the impact on the community’s health and safety will be substantial. She expressed gratitude to the city departments and the community for their patience and dedication to realizing this vision, marking the vote as a major milestone after years of discussion.

Councilman Brooks acknowledged Councilwoman Kenneth’s work, noting that the project is in his district and that he had been collaborating with his predecessor, Councilwoman Monteiro, on the initiative. He thanked her for her contributions. Another council member, who previously toured the site with the Greenway Foundation, expressed excitement about the project’s completion after a long wait.

The meeting then transitioned to the next agenda item, with the Secretary of the Council preparing to display the document for Councilwoman Ortega’s comment. The primary decision recorded was the council’s engagement with the grant agreement to facilitate the creation of the new natural open space in Globeville.
